== Overview & Architectural Fit ==
'''SpECTRE''' evolves the equations of relativistic astrophysics (mergers of black holes and neutron stars, supernovae) with a task-based discontinuous Galerkin and spectral-element method, written in C++ on Charm++. It solves systems in the conservation form <math>\partial_t u + \partial_i F^i(u) = S(u)</math> to high order on many processors.

== Mathematical Evaluation for TPM ==
* '''Lagrangian / Action (1.5/10):''' Evolves fixed formulations and takes no action as input.
* '''Field / PDE (8.5/10):''' High-order and massively parallel.
* '''Relativity (9/10):''' A strong-field relativity code.
* '''Quantum / Data (1.5/10):''' Little quantum or data focus.

== Integration Pipeline ==
# '''Reduce''' the container's action-derived gravity to general relativity in the limit of interest.
# '''Take''' SpECTRE's (and the [[The Principia Machina/Tools/EinsteinToolkit|Einstein Toolkit]]'s) solutions and waveforms as the trusted benchmark for that limit, compared only after the derivation (quarantine).
# '''For a new theory''', a well-posed hyperbolic formulation must exist first, then be implemented in C++.

== Status, Licence and Limits ==
* '''Status:''' Very active, releases about monthly; the latest, v2026.09.05 of 6 September 2026, has a Zenodo DOI.
* '''Licence:''' MIT.
* '''Home:''' https://spectre-code.org
* '''Limits:''' The Charm++ build and its high-performance computing needs are heavy. It consumes action-derived equations; it never produces them.

== On the Principia Machina ==
A tool runs only where the sponsor installed and bound it, and what it returns is untrusted input, vetted before use; its numbers are never values of the site's calculator, TPC. A value it computes lands as a RESULT with QUANTITY, VALUE, UNIT and AT, its initial and boundary values as SITUATION records; the regime of a numerical result, and whether such a value may be presented, are open questions of the specification. See [[The Principia Machina/Agent/Tools|Agent/Tools]] and [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Operator's guide|the operator's guide]].
